plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional illustration of a positively charged particle following a helical path in a uniform magnetic field. Three axes meet at the origin O, with x running to the right, y upward, and z toward the lower left, and a small orange sphere labeled q sits at the origin. From the particle, a green arrow labeled 'v perp' points straight up along y, a short arrow labeled 'v para' points along the x direction, and a green arrow labeled 'v' between the two gives the total velocity. A blue arrow labeled with a vector B lies along the positive x-axis, and a red arrow labeled 'F' is drawn at the particle. An orange helix of roughly three turns occupies the right side of the frame, each loop circling in the plane perpendicular to x with small arrowheads on the coils marking the sense of rotation, and successive loops shifted steadily in the positive x direction. Above the coils a short green double-headed arrow labeled 'v para' spans the gap between two consecutive turns. Splitting the velocity into two components makes visible which part bends the trajectory and which part carries the particle forward. The drawing shows how a velocity oblique to the field yields circular motion superposed on uniform travel along it.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an axonometric textbook-style 3D diagram with no perspective convergence. World-space scale: origin at (0,0,0); +X is screen-right and is the magnetic-field/helix axis; +Y is screen-up; +Z recedes toward lower-left. Draw x-axis from x=-0.2 to x=6.2, y-axis from y=0 to y=3.9, and z-axis from z=0 to z=2.5, all black with arrowheads. Place the orange charge q as a sphere of radius about 0.16 at the origin, color #f26a21 with a yellow-orange highlight. The blue B arrow lies on +X from x=0.15 to x=1.75, color #1f77b4, label as vector B. Velocity arrows originate at or very near q: v_perp length about 1.25 along +Y in green #6aa84f; v_para length proportional to the vParallel slider along +X in the same green; total v is the vector sum, drawn diagonally in the XY plane from the particle. Force F for a positive charge with v_perp initially +Y and B along +X points along -Z; because +Z is drawn lower-left, -Z appears up/right from the particle, color red #d62728. Helix centerline follows +X slightly to the right of the particle; draw about 3 turns from x≈0.45 to x≈5.4. Use parametric path x(t)=v_parallel*t, y(t)=r*sin(omega*t), z(t)=r*cos(omega*t)-r so the path begins near the particle and initially has upward velocity; choose omega=1 in display units and r=v_perp/omega scaled so default r≈0.95. Pitch per turn = 2*pi*v_parallel/omega, scaled so the default pitch is about 1.35 world units; rescale the visible x-length to keep roughly three turns in frame. Helix color is bright orange #ff6600, thin tube or thick line. Add 3 small orange cone arrowheads tangent to the helix at visible front/right portions of successive coils. The pitch indicator is a green double-headed arrow above the helix between two adjacent turns, parallel to +X, labeled v_para. Text labels should match the source: italic/vector styling where possible, with v_perp left of the vertical arrow, v_para beside the short horizontal arrow near the particle and again above the pitch arrow, v beside the diagonal green arrow, F beside the red arrow, and B below or beside the blue field arrow.
interactionPlan.notes: Animate a small glowing particle along the helix while keeping a faint full orange trajectory visible. Recompute helix geometry, tangent arrowheads, pitch bracket, and velocity-component arrows whenever either slider changes. Use billboarded text sprites so labels remain readable in the axonometric pose. For physical consistency with a uniform B field, keep cyclotron angular frequency omega fixed for fixed q/m and B; v_perp changes radius and tangential speed, while v_parallel changes pitch.

authoredContext:
The result is a helical motion, as shown in the following figure.

A charged particle moving with a velocity not in the same direction as the magnetic field. The velocity component perpendicular to the magnetic field creates circular motion, whereas the component of the velocity parallel to the field moves the particle along a straight line. The pitch is the horizontal distance between two consecutive circles. The resulting motion is helical.

An illustration of a positively charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field. The field is in the positive x direction. The initial velocity is shown as having a component, v sub para, in the positive x direction and another component, v sub perp, in the positive y direction. The particle moves in a helix that loops in the y z plane (counterclockwise from the particle’s perspective) and advances in the positive x direction.

While the charged particle travels in a helical path, it may enter a region where the magnetic field is not uniform. In particular, suppose a particle travels from a region of strong magnetic field to a region of weaker field, then back to a region of stronger field. The particle may reflect back before entering the stronger magnetic field region. This is similar to a wave on a string traveling from a very light, thin string to a hard wall and reflecting backward. If the reflection happens at both ends, the particle is trapped in a so-called magnetic bottle.

Three axes meet at the origin O, with x running to the right, y upward, and z toward the lower left, and a small orange sphere labeled q sits at the origin. From the particle, a green arrow labeled 'v perp' points straight up along y, a short arrow labeled 'v para' points along the x direction, and a green arrow labeled 'v' between the two gives the total velocity. A blue arrow labeled with a vector B lies along the positive x-axis, and a red arrow labeled 'F' is drawn at the particle. An orange helix of roughly three turns occupies the right side of the frame, each loop circling in the plane perpendicular to x with small arrowheads on the coils marking the sense of rotation, and successive loops shifted steadily in the positive x direction. Above the coils a short green double-headed arrow labeled 'v para' spans the gap between two consecutive turns. Splitting the velocity into two components makes visible which part bends the trajectory and which part carries the particle forward. The drawing shows how a velocity oblique to the field yields circular motion superposed on uniform travel along it.

elements: three coordinate axes meeting at origin O: x-axis horizontal to the right, y-axis vertical upward, z-axis receding diagonally toward the lower left
arrowheads at positive ends of x, y, and z axes
axis labels x, y, z
origin label O just left of the particle
small orange charged-particle sphere at the origin labeled q
blue magnetic-field vector B starting at the particle and pointing along positive x
green perpendicular-velocity vector v_perp starting at the particle and pointing upward along positive y
green parallel-velocity vector v_para starting at the particle and pointing right along positive x
green total-velocity vector v starting at the particle and pointing diagonally between v_perp and v_para
red magnetic-force vector F starting near the particle and pointing diagonally toward negative z, screen-up/right relative to the positive-z axis
orange helical trajectory extending from the particle region to the right along the positive x-axis
approximately three orange circular turns of the helix in planes perpendicular to the x-axis
small orange arrowheads on the helix showing the sense of rotation
short green double-headed pitch arrow above the coils spanning the x-distance between adjacent turns
label v_para above the pitch arrow
labels v_perp, v_para, v, F, and vector B positioned near their respective arrows

interactions.label: Animate particle motion
interactions.teaches: The charged particle's motion is the superposition of circular gyration from the perpendicular velocity and steady translation along the magnetic-field direction from the parallel velocity

interactions.label: v_parallel
interactions.teaches: Changing the velocity component parallel to B stretches or compresses the helix pitch while leaving the circular radius unchanged

interactions.label: v_perp
interactions.teaches: Changing the velocity component perpendicular to B changes the gyration radius and circular motion around the field line while leaving the forward axial advance set by v_parallel

demo_steps.title: Oblique velocity creates a helix
demo_steps.narration: With both velocity components present, the orange path wraps around the magnetic-field direction while advancing to the right. The green vector v is the sum of v_perp and v_parallel.

demo_steps.title: Increase v_parallel
demo_steps.narration: The spacing between successive coils increases, but the coil radius stays fixed. This shows that the parallel component controls how far the particle travels along B during each gyration.

demo_steps.title: Increase v_perp
demo_steps.narration: The helix grows wider while its axial advance rate is unchanged. This isolates the perpendicular component as the part of the velocity responsible for circular bending.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an axonometric textbook-style 3D diagram with no perspective convergence. World-space scale: origin at (0,0,0); +X is screen-right and is the magnetic-field/helix axis; +Y is screen-up; +Z recedes toward lower-left. Draw x-axis from x=-0.2 to x=6.2, y-axis from y=0 to y=3.9, and z-axis from z=0 to z=2.5, all black with arrowheads. Place the orange charge q as a sphere of radius about 0.16 at the origin, color #f26a21 with a yellow-orange highlight. The blue B arrow lies on +X from x=0.15 to x=1.75, color #1f77b4, label as vector B. Velocity arrows originate at or very near q: v_perp length about 1.25 along +Y in green #6aa84f; v_para length proportional to the vParallel slider along +X in the same green; total v is the vector sum, drawn diagonally in the XY plane from the particle. Force F for a positive charge with v_perp initially +Y and B along +X points along -Z; because +Z is drawn lower-left, -Z appears up/right from the particle, color red #d62728. Helix centerline follows +X slightly to the right of the particle; draw about 3 turns from x≈0.45 to x≈5.4. Use parametric path x(t)=v_parallel*t, y(t)=r*sin(omega*t), z(t)=r*cos(omega*t)-r so the path begins near the particle and initially has upward velocity; choose omega=1 in display units and r=v_perp/omega scaled so default r≈0.95. Pitch per turn = 2*pi*v_parallel/omega, scaled so the default pitch is about 1.35 world units; rescale the visible x-length to keep roughly three turns in frame. Helix color is bright orange #ff6600, thin tube or thick line. Add 3 small orange cone arrowheads tangent to the helix at visible front/right portions of successive coils. The pitch indicator is a green double-headed arrow above the helix between two adjacent turns, parallel to +X, labeled v_para. Text labels should match the source: italic/vector styling where possible, with v_perp left of the vertical arrow, v_para beside the short horizontal arrow near the particle and again above the pitch arrow, v beside the diagonal green arrow, F beside the red arrow, and B below or beside the blue field arrow.
interactionPlan.notes: Animate a small glowing particle along the helix while keeping a faint full orange trajectory visible. Recompute helix geometry, tangent arrowheads, pitch bracket, and velocity-component arrows whenever either slider changes. Use billboarded text sprites so labels remain readable in the axonometric pose. For physical consistency with a uniform B field, keep cyclotron angular frequency omega fixed for fixed q/m and B; v_perp changes radius and tangential speed, while v_parallel changes pitch.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for particle motion: the learner starts the simulation, the charged particle circles while advancing along the magnetic-field axis, showing that perpendicular velocity creates rotation and parallel velocity creates translation.
- Slider for v_parallel: the learner increases the component along B, the helix pitch stretches while the loop radius stays fixed, clarifying how forward speed sets spacing between turns.
- Slider for v_perp: the learner changes the perpendicular component, the circular radius and rotation speed update while axial advance is unchanged, showing which velocity component controls the gyration around the field line.

discrepancies: The orange helical path is drawn as widely separated coils, while the source shows tighter, overlapping elliptical loops around the x-directed magnetic-field axis.
The helix begins noticeably to the right of the charge rather than appearing to emerge immediately from q as in the source.
The red force vector is too short and visually obscured compared with the clearly visible up-right red F arrow in the source.
The initial x-axis view is slightly slanted rather than nearly horizontal, making the projection less faithful to the textbook diagram.
evaluation.notes: The figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually correct, with useful interactions, but the helix spacing/start position and force-vector prominence differ from the source.
action_items: Tighten the helix pitch so the coils overlap more like the source figure.
Move the start of the helical trajectory closer to q so it appears to originate at the particle.
Make the red F arrow longer and less hidden behind the velocity arrows.
Adjust the camera so the x-axis is closer to horizontal while keeping y vertical and z down-left.
